name: Zoji La
connects: Srinagar (Kashmir Valley) with Kargil and Leh (Ladakh)
strategicSignificance: Vital lifeline connecting the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh along National Highway 1 (NH-1). Recaptured by Indian Army in Operation Bison (1948) using tanks at high altitude.
examFacts: Zoji La Tunnel (14.15 km under construction) will be India and Asia's longest bi-directional road tunnel, providing all-weather connectivity.
Historically famous for Operation Bison in November 1948 where Stuart light tanks were used at over 11,500 feet elevation for the first time in world military history.
Marks the transition zone between the lush temperate Kashmir Valley and the cold arid rain-shadow Ladakh plateau.

name: Rohtang Pass
connects: Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys of Himachal Pradesh
strategicSignificance: Ancient trade route between Kullu and Central Asia. The 9.02 km Atal Tunnel beneath the pass provides round-the-year military and civilian transit.
examFacts: Name literally means 'pile of corpses' in Tibetan due to frequent killer blizzards and extreme weather.
The Atal Tunnel (9.02 km) was built under the Rohtang Pass at 3,100 m elevation, bypasses snow closures and reduces distance between Manali and Keylong by 46 km.
Acts as a watershed divide between the Chenab River basin (Chandra/Bhaga) and the Beas River basin.

name: Shipki La
connects: Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh with Tibet (Ngari Prefecture, China)
strategicSignificance: The perennial antecedent Sutlej River enters India from Tibet through a deep gorge near Shipki La.
examFacts: Sutlej River (originating from Lake Rakshastal near Mount Kailash in Tibet) pierces the Himalayas and enters India near Shipki La.
One of India's official border trade posts with China along with Nathu La (Sikkim) and Lipulekh (Uttarakhand).
Branch of the ancient Silk Road route into the Sutlej valley.

name: Bara-lacha La
strategicSignificance: Crucial high mountain pass along the Manali-Leh Highway. Source of both the Chandra and Bhaga rivers.
examFacts: The Chandra River originates from a glacier on the south-east side and the Bhaga River originates from Suraj Tal lake near this pass.
Their confluence downstream at Tandi forms the Chandrabhaga River, known as the Chenab in Jammu & Kashmir.
Suraj Tal (Sun Lake), the third highest lake in India, is situated just below the pass.

name: Lipulekh Pass
connects: Pithoragarh (Uttarakhand, India) with Purang / Taklakot (Tibet, China)
strategicSignificance: Located at the tri-junction of India, Nepal, and China. Primary overland transit pass for the annual official Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra.
examFacts: First Indian border pass opened for trading with China in 1992 following bilateral agreements.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) conducts the annual Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra pilgrimage through Lipulekh Pass.
Part of the Kalapani territorial dispute claimed by Nepal under the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli.

name: Mana Pass (Dungri La)
strategicSignificance: One of the highest vehicle-accessible motorable mountain passes in the world; guarded by ITBP and Indian Army.
examFacts: Mana is famously celebrated as the 'First Village of India' (formerly the last Indian village before the border with Tibet).
Source of the Saraswati River, a tributary of the Alaknanda joining at Keshav Prayag in Mana.
Deo Tal lake near Mana Pass is considered a primary source of the Saraswati River.

name: Nathu La
connects: Gangtok (Sikkim, India) with the Chumbi Valley and Yadong (Tibet, China)
strategicSignificance: Ancient branch of the Silk Route. Site of the 1967 Nathu La and Cho La clashes where the Indian Army successfully repulsed PLA aggression.
examFacts: Reopened for bilateral border trade in July 2006 following prime ministerial agreements between India and China.
Alternative pilgrimage route for the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra, offering a motorable path compared to trekking through Lipulekh.
Strategic proximity to the narrow Siliguri Corridor ('Chicken's Neck') via the adjacent Chumbi Valley and Doklam Plateau.

name: Jelep La
connects: Kalimpong / Sikkim with Lhasa (Tibet) through the Menmecho Lake and Chumbi Valley
strategicSignificance: Historic trade route for wool trade between Tibet and Bengal prior to the 1962 Sino-Indian War.
examFacts: Name 'Jelep La' in Tibetan translates to 'The Lovely Level Pass'.
The historic Younghusband Expedition to Lhasa (1903-04) marched through this pass.
Menmecho Lake lies just below Jelep La and gives rise to the Rangpo River, tributary of the Teesta.

name: Bomdi La
connects: Tezpur (Assam) and the Brahmaputra Plains with the Tawang Valley
strategicSignificance: Key military gateway to Tawang near the McMahon Line; site of heavy fighting in the 1962 conflict.
examFacts: Provides strategic access to the historic Tawang Monastery (India's largest Buddhist monastery and second largest in the world after the Potala Palace).
The Sela Pass (4,170 m) with the newly inaugurated Sela Tunnel lies further north on this highway toward Tawang.
Forms the cultural transition from the plains of Assam to Monpa Tibetan Buddhist culture.

name: Diphu Pass
connects: Arunachal Pradesh (India), Tibet (China), and Kachin State (Myanmar)
strategicSignificance: Strategic tri-junction of India, China, and Myanmar on the McMahon Line.
examFacts: Provides a natural low-altitude passage across the Indo-Myanmar border to the Irrawaddy basin.
Strategic point on the McMahon Line where border perceptions between India, Myanmar, and China converge.

name: Banihal Pass
connects: Jammu (Outer Plains) with the Kashmir Valley (Srinagar)
strategicSignificance: Historically bridged by the 2.85 km Jawahar Tunnel (opened in 1956) and the new Banihal-Qazigund four-lane double-tube tunnel (8.45 km).
examFacts: The 11.2 km Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel (T-80) passes underneath this pass, connecting Banihal in Jammu with Qazigund in Kashmir (India's longest transportation railway tunnel until recent Rishikesh-Karanprayag developments).
Connects the Chenab valley with the Jhelum valley.
Name 'Banihal' means blizzard in Kashmiri.

name: Thal Ghat (Kasara Ghat)
connects: Mumbai with Nashik, Dhule, and the northern/eastern railway corridors (Kolkata/Delhi)
strategicSignificance: Critical mountain pass carrying the Mumbai-Agra National Highway (NH-3) and the Central Railway trunk line over the steep Sahyadri scarp.
examFacts: Engineered with reversing stations and steep gradients requiring banker locomotives for railway trains climbing from Kasara to Igatpuri.
Gateway for trade between the Konkan coast (Mumbai port) and the northern Deccan plateau.
Rain-shadow transition where the humid Konkan climate abruptly shifts to the semi-arid dry plateau of Nashik.

name: Bhor Ghat (Khandala Ghat)
connects: Mumbai with Pune, Bengaluru, and Chennai across the Western Ghats
strategicSignificance: Carries the Mumbai-Pune Expressway (India's first access-controlled toll expressway) and the Central Railway line to southern India.
examFacts: Historically famous for the Battle of Wadgaon (1779) in the First Anglo-Maratha War, where Maratha forces under Mahadji Shinde routed the British East India Company.
One of the steepest rail ascents in the world between Karjat and Lonavala (1 in 37 incline).
Archaeologically rich with nearby ancient Karla Caves and Bhaja Caves on the Buddhist trade route.

name: Palghat Gap (Palakkad Gap)
strategicSignificance: A major 30 km wide structural discontinuity / geological shear zone in the continuous chain of the Western Ghats, located between the Nilgiri Hills in the north and the Anaimalai Hills in the south.
examFacts: Low elevation (~140 m) break that allows moisture-laden South-West Monsoon winds to penetrate into western Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore region).
Major transportation artery carrying NH-544 and Southern Railway lines linking Kerala with the rest of India.
Geologically formed as a shear fracture during the separation of India and Madagascar in the late Cretaceous.

name: Shencottah Gap
connects: Kollam / Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala) with Madurai / Tirunelveli (Tamil Nadu)
strategicSignificance: Natural break in the southern Sahyadris separating the Cardamom Hills from the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve.
examFacts: Oldest railway connection between Travancore state and Madras Presidency, opened in 1904.
NH-744 passes through this gap, facilitating interstate vegetable, fruit, and spice commerce between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

name: Haldighati Pass
connects: Rajsamand and Udaipur across the rugged Aravalli ridges
strategicSignificance: Historic narrow mountain pass where the Battle of Haldighati took place on 18 June 1576 between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and Mughal forces led by Raja Man Singh I of Amber.
examFacts: Named 'Haldighati' because the yellow-colored turmeric-like soil (Haldi) of the mountain ridge.
Famous memorial to Maharana Pratap's loyal warhorse Chetak located near the pass.
Acts as a defensive natural bastion in the oldest fold mountain system in India (Aravallis).
